title: A closed subset meeting the generic fibre meets all nearby fibres
statement: Let h:P\to T be finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let eta be a generic point of all of T, and let C be a closed subset of P. If C intersect h^{-1}({eta}) is nonempty, there is an open V containing eta such that C intersect h^{-1}({t}) is nonempty for every t in V. The set-theoretic fibres agree with the images of the scheme fibres [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. No noetherianity, reducedness, or separatedness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 055G, nonempty-intersection image argument; Tags 052A and 01UA.

proof.text: Base change along the reduction of the irreducible base T. Give the inverse image of C its reduced closed subscheme structure. A closed immersion is locally finite type and quasi-compact, so its composite to the integral base is finite type. The generic fibre is nonempty by the hypothesis and the reduction homeomorphism.

Tag 052A supplies a nonempty affine open of the integral base on which the reduced closed subscheme map is flat and of finite presentation. Tag 01UA makes its image open. This image contains the generic point because its fibre there is nonempty. On that image every fibre meets the closed subscheme. Transfer the image-open to T via its reduction homeomorphism to get V and the claimed set-theoretic nonemptiness.
